title: Cristaux et cohomologie de De Rham : généralités, correspondances Deligne et Berthelot (1965-1969) : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (previous page): Grothendieck compares several 'de Rham-type' sites attached to X/S: Zariski, DR, DR_strat (a 'stratifying' de Rham site), Strat, and Cris. If X is formally smooth over S, the vertical comparison arrows are equivalences. In characteristic 0 the horizontal ones are. In DR_strat the object X~ (the sheaf associated to X) covers the final object. So there is a Cech/Leray spectral sequence E_2^{pq} = H^p(nu -> H^q(X~^{nu+1}, O)) converging to H^*(X_{DR_str}, O).

This page computes the terms of that spectral sequence.
(1) The fibre product X~^{nu+1} in the topos is ind-representable, as follows.
- On X^{(nu)} := X^{nu+1}, take the infinitesimal neighbourhoods Delta^{(nu)}_{X/S}(i) of the (small) diagonal, for i >= 0.
- Each is augmented to Delta(0) = X via O_{Delta(i)} -> O_X.
- Take the divided-power envelope of the augmentation ideal; this is the augmented PD object, written Delta(i)~. Grothendieck notes the tilde notation is consistent with its earlier use for 'associated sheaf'.
- Truncate it at PD-order j, giving Delta(i)(j). Then Delta(i)~ = colim_j Delta(i)(j), and X~^{nu+1} = colim_{i,j} Delta^{(nu)}_{X/S}(i)(j).
- In modern terms, X~^{nu+1} is the formal PD-envelope (PD-hull) of the diagonal X -> X^{nu+1}, presented as an ind-scheme.
(2) Marked 'à vérifier': for any object (U,U') of the site, the localized topos has H^q(DRst/(U,U'), O) = H^q(U', O_{U'}).

The next page draws the consequences.
- For X affine, H^q(X~^{nu+1}, O) = 0 for q > 0, and H^0 = lim_{i,j} of the coordinate rings of Delta(i)(j). So H^n(X_{DRstrat}, O) is the cohomology of the cosimplicial ring nu -> (completed PD-envelope of the diagonal in X^{nu+1}).
- Globalising, one gets an O_X-augmented cosimplicial ring E^* of PD-envelopes of the diagonals, with H^*(X_{DRstrat}, O) = H^*(X_Zar, E^*).

This is the Cech-Alexander / 'PD-stratification' computation of crystalline-type cohomology by the cosimplicial PD-hulls D_{X/S}(nu) of the diagonals. Its linearization gives the PD-de Rham complex when X is smooth.
errors: The ind-presentation is plausible but stated without verification. The step H^q(localized topos, O) = H^q(U', O_{U'}) is explicitly flagged 'à vérifier'. It relies on objects of DR_strat being such that the localized topos is equivalent to Zariski sheaves on U'.

For X not smooth over S, the PD-envelope of the diagonal of X itself (rather than of a smooth ambient embedding) need not compute crystalline cohomology in char p. The resulting 'stratifying' cohomology is a different invariant. The page does not discuss this; it is only consistent with the formally smooth case noted on the previous page.
Notation shifts between tilde and hat (X~^{nu+1} here, X-hat on the next page): a sheaf/ind-object vs. a formal completion. This is harmless but imprecise.

ideas.what: Cech/Leray spectral sequence for the covering X~ -> final object in the (PD-)stratifying de Rham topos
ideas.modern_name: Cech-Alexander complex computation of crystalline cohomology
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Crystals and de Rham cohomology, 1966/68); Berthelot (Cohomologie cristalline, 1974); modern treatment Bhatt-de Jong (2011), Stacks Project
ideas.where_published: Possibly in 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' (Dix exposés, 1968) in the discussion of stratifications; unsure of exact form

ideas.what: Fibre powers of X~ are ind-represented by PD-envelopes Delta(i)(j) of the infinitesimal neighbourhoods of the diagonal
ideas.modern_name: PD-envelope of the diagonal D_{X/S}(nu) and its PD-filtration truncations; PD-stratifications
ideas.where_published: Analogous non-PD version (infinitesimal neighbourhoods P^n of the diagonal, stratifications) in EGA IV 16 and 'Crystals' (Dix exposés)

ideas.what: Cohomology of DR_strat computed as Zariski hypercohomology of an O_X-augmented cosimplicial ring E^* of PD-hulls (next page)

missed.claim: Grothendieck works with a 'PD-stratifying de Rham site' DR_strat intermediate between DR and Cris. Its cohomology for non-smooth X is computed by cosimplicial PD-envelopes of the diagonal of X itself. For singular X this is a distinct invariant, related to but not identical with crystalline cohomology. Its systematic study does not seem standard, though it is close to existing notions.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Marginal. Compare with Bhatt's derived de Rham / derived crystalline cohomology and Cech-Alexander complexes for singular schemes. This is likely already absorbed into the literature.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a standard early version of the Cech-Alexander computation of crystalline-type cohomology via PD-envelopes of diagonals. That machinery was developed by Berthelot and is well known. The DR_strat variant and the double ind-presentation (i,j) are a minor archival detail.
transcription_corrections: Margin note at the bottom left reads '29 / à vérifier' (page number plus 'to be checked' for the displayed isomorphism), not part of the formula.

'un des puissances divisées' in the bracketed passage is probably 'le voisinage [d'ordre j au sens] des puissances divisées' — i.e. the PD-neighbourhood of order j; the crossed-out words are illegible.
The underbrace label reads approximately 'faisceau DP-stratifiant "représenté" par Delta(i) augmenté vers Delta(0)', with 'faisceau DR-' corrected to 'DP-'.
In the last line, 'DRst' is written over a crossed-out 'DRstr'; the formula reads H^q(DRst~/(U,U')~ ; O) ≅ H^q(U', O_{U'}).
